findings_addressed.oracle: bridge.get_alignment_grid() called directly on the registered HexEditorBridge instance returns the value set via dispatch; if execute_tool_call routes to the wrong bridge the oracle stays at 0 while the dispatched value is 512
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In tools.py execute_tool_call(), change `bridge = self._bridges.get(tool_enum)` to `bridge = list(self._bridges.values())[0]` — the dispatch reaches a different bridge, oracle stays at 0, assert oracle_grid == 512 fails

notes: Added _ALIGNMENT_GRID_SIZE constant (512). After the three existing storage/retrieval assertions, the test now dispatches set_alignment_grid(size=512) via execute_tool_call (driving the full dispatch path: tool-name normalisation, bridge lookup, capability gate, attribute resolution, coroutine dispatch) and asserts the return value is True. The independent oracle is bridge.get_alignment_grid() called directly on the registered instance, which must equal 512. A final execute_tool_call of get_alignment_grid verifies the round-trip. Any broken routing, wrong-bridge dispatch, or attribute-resolution regression leaves the oracle at 0 while the assertion expects 512.
